# Shared reth dependency updates

The nightly updater uses the shared dependency-update workflow from
[gh-actions#338](https://github.com/tempoxyz/gh-actions/pull/338), pinned to its
reviewed draft commit. Merge that dependency first and repin to its final release
before enabling this migration.

`scripts/prepare_reth_update.py` resolves upstream reth main to a full SHA,
compares it with Tempo main's resolved pin, and updates Cargo manifest pins.
The shared workflow owns lockfile resolution, bounded local/CI repair, explicit
leased pushes, and just-in-time STS publication. It resumes `reth-auto-bump`,
preserves source migrations, and fails on rebase conflicts instead of selecting
a side. Rust, manifest, and lockfile changes are allowed; Git/configuration and
submodule pointers stay frozen. No deployment or auto-merge is requested.

## Enablement

1. Merge the shared implementation and both caller STS policies to main. Ensure
   the STS App is installed with contents/PR write, without branch-rule bypass.
2. Create the `dependency-updates` environment, restricted to main. Provide
   `AMP_API_KEY` there or through the explicitly forwarded repository secret.
   Configure environment approvals according to the desired unattended policy.
3. Set `UPDATE_RETH_WORKER_IMAGE` to a reviewed, digest-pinned Linux image
   (`ghcr.io/...@sha256:...`). It needs Amp, stable
   Rust, nightly-2026-10-02 with Clippy/rustfmt, cargo-nextest, zepter, and native
   build dependencies. Tools must work without root writes; Cargo/Amp writable
   state lives in `/cache`. Set image defaults such as `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4` and
   `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1700000000` to match Tempo CI. The image must be publicly
   pullable or preloaded on the runner; no registry credentials enter workers.
4. Manually dispatch on main and review the resulting PR before leaving the
   nightly schedule enabled. Until the image variable exists, the update job
   skips. This draft does not provision the image, environment, secrets or App.

The publishing policy trusts the immutable Tempo repository/environment subject,
its main caller workflow, and the pinned shared workflow. Tokens last at most
15 minutes and are revoked before returning to repair. Follow-ups have a separate
PR-write-only policy; `DEREK_UPDATE_RETH_TOKEN` is no longer used by this workflow.

## Follow-ups

After the configured lint, test, specs, dependency, publishing and semver
workflows pass for the candidate SHA, the caller adds dependency/Cyclops labels.
Existing `pr-audit.yml` handles the audit; the upstream comparison and audit
scope are recorded in the PR body rather than generated by another Amp call.

The caller invokes the existing `bench-e2e.yml` directly for the tip20 comparison
at the exact repaired SHA. This avoids granting the STS bot an exception to the
human-member comment dispatcher. Benchmark settings and its own Slack/reporting
remain in that reusable workflow. Update/follow-up failures alert reth on-call.
The existing reth-bump candidate-image workflow remains unchanged.

Live worker/STS/benchmark integration remains a manual enablement check.
